entries.title: Everything You Need to Know for Commanders-Niners
entries.summary: How to watch, pregame reading and more for Monday night’s game.
entries.content:
The Commanders travel across the country to face the undefeated Niners on Monday Night Football, a week after depriving themselves of a chance at a win against the Giants and settling for a tie.

Here’s everything you need to know.

Kickoff: 8:15 p.m. ET at Levi’s Stadium, Santa Clara, California

TV: ABC and ESPN

Betting Lines

Lines from DraftKings, as of Friday. 

Spread: Commanders +7.5

Money line: Commanders +330, 49ers -425

Over/under: 51.5 points

Pregame Reading

The Packers’ star pass rusher Micah Parsons, who played for Commanders coach Dan Quinn in Dallas when Quinn was the Cowboys’ defensive coordinator, blamed Sunday’s tie and overtime gaffe solely on quarterback Jayden Daniels. Parsons said his former coach will be out of a job because of Daniels.

The Commanders’ lack of clock management in overtime against the Giants cost them a victory. Columnist Thomas Boswell wrote about the mistakes made in the waning seconds.

How do players move on from such a disappointing result? The Commanders coped with a mix of family time, pumpkin patches and romantic comedies, Martenzie Johnson reports.

About the Niners

The vibes are good in the Bay Area. The Niners are 5-0 and looking to upgrade their roster ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline. General manager John Lynch, one of the more aggressive in-season executives, recently said star tight end George Kittle is lobbying him to trade for Chargers defensive end Khalil Mack.

The Niners are winning despite a banged-up wide receiver room. Deebo Samuel (hamstring), Demarcus Robinson (ankle sprain), and rookie De’Zhaun Stribling (ankle surgery) are all out for multiple weeks. But the team opened the practice window on Thursday for nine-year veteran Christian Kirk, who’s coming off a calf injury. Mike Evans, who’s battling a rib injury and Achilles soreness, is expected to play on Monday.

The game will also feature an on-field family reunion. Niners star running back Christian McCaffrey is the older brother of Commanders wideout Luke McCaffrey. Luke is the youngest of the four McCaffrey brothers, whose father, Ed, won three Super Bowls as a wide receiver. The two will play each other for the first time in the NFL.

“He's the only brother I've never gotten to play with or against, so I think this completes the cycle of sharing the field with him,” Christian McCaffrey told The San Jose Mercury News.

One Big Question

Can the Commanders move on from last week?

The Commanders’ end-of-game ridiculousness dominated most of the NFL news cycle this week, and even though the game didn’t result in a loss, Quinn said it felt like one. It’s the kind of game that can hang over a team for weeks.

Can Quinn and Daniels find a way to move the Commanders forward? While 1-3-1 isn’t an ideal record five games in, 12 more remain — including a stretch of winnable matchups in the back half of their schedule.

Quote of the Week

“I let guys know it'll never happen again, and we’re going to move forward,” Daniels said he told his teammates during a meeting on Monday.

Daniels took full responsibility for the tie, absolving Quinn and offensive coordinator David Blough for their roles in the overtime-clock mismanagement. Daniels looked great in his return from his second elbow dislocation in as many seasons, completing 68% of his passes for 199 yards and rushing for 103 yards and two touchdowns.

entries.title: The Spirit Has Plenty to Celebrate After a Home Win Against Gotham FC
entries.summary: Despite recent struggles at Audi Field, Washington kept its NWSL Shield hopes alive with a 1-0 win over the league leaders.
entries.content:
As the crowd roared and fireworks filled the sky, groups of players and coaches exchanged hugs before making their way to the stands to celebrate with their fans.

That type of scene has become exceedingly rare for Washington Spirit supporters of late, as the team had lost five of its last six games at Audi Field ahead of Saturday’s meeting with Gotham FC.

So the Spirit would’ve had reason to savor a victory against any team in any manner at home. But on Saturday, Washington gave itself plenty to celebrate as it earned a marquee 1-0 win over its bitter rivals and the league leaders, clinching a spot in the playoffs for the third consecutive year and keeping its NWSL Shield hopes alive.

“It's a really nice feeling to finally stand in front of the crowd and stand in front of [the media] and have that feeling of, ‘Okay, job accomplished,’” defender Gabrielle Carle said. “We've come short so many games in a row now and I think this one was really important for us, of course to clinch [playoffs], but just as a confidence builder … this one was huge for us.”

Coach Adrián González said the Spirit’s performance was probably its best of the season, with Lucia Di Guglielmo’s 70th-minute goal lifting Washington to back-to-back victories for just the second time since the beginning of August. The result also snapped a five-game streak without a win in regulation against Gotham FC, dating back to June 2024.

“Today we wanted to feel that joy, that energy, that feeling that we are able to beat any team,” González said. “It's important for us, for the club, for the fans to have a performance like this, and also clinching playoffs for the third season in a row, it’s not easy.”

“Doing it here at home with your people against a great opponent, and also seeing where we were coming from, I think it’s huge. Everyone deserves to have a game like this — the players, the team, staff, fans,” he said.

The victory leaves Washington just three points off first-place Gotham and two points behind second-place San Diego Wave FC with two regular season games remaining.

The Spirit looked the more dangerous team from the start of Saturday’s game. The return of attacking midfielder Leicy Santos, who missed eight matches with an injury, provided a massive boost to an offense that has struggled in her absence. Santos was influential throughout a first half that saw Washington outshoot Gotham FC eight to four, with Trinity Rodman forcing a pair of key saves from Gotham goalkeeper Ann-Katrin Berger.

Forward Clara Luvanga also made an impact in her first start for the Spirit. She blazed her best chance over the crossbar early on Saturday but provided a target for the Spirit to find directly out of the back, often winning the first ball and gradually improving her hold-up play throughout the match.

“We approached the game with a really strong aggression and that kind of set the tone,” defender Esme Morgan said. “We did a good job out of possession, being front-footed and winning the ball back in their half. And I think with the ball, we did a good job of finding the forward players.”

Mélissa Bethi replaced Santos to start the second half and made the difference for the Spirit after taking some time to get up to game speed. Washington won the ball high up the pitch and, after Gotham rebuffed the Spirit’s first attempt to play through its defense, Bethi’s clipped ball found the advanced run of Di Guglielmo, who calmly took a touch and found the bottom corner in the 70th minute. It was the fullback’s first goal for the Spirit.

“I really felt this game, and this is because of the team, because they made me feel this rivalry,” Di Guglielmo said. “My first goal today is because of all the work I did and we did during the whole season, so I'm really happy, of course, that happened today. It's kind of a dream.”

Bethi nearly doubled Washington’s lead three minutes later, hitting the crossbar from a shot just outside the penalty box. Santos and Bethi’s contributions to a strong team performance are a very positive sign for Washington, which has largely lacked a true attacking midfielder during their recent inconsistent stretch.

“She's such a special player,” Carle said of Bethi. “As you've seen on the goal, she has an eye for what's about to happen, she just sees the play develop before it's even developed.”

The Spirit’s defensive performance matched the energy of its rejuvenated offense. Washington earned its 11th clean sheet of the season by preventing a Gotham team stacked with attacking talent from producing any big chances despite handling a majority of possession.

The Spirit has struggled against Gotham since 2024, failing to score in one draw and three losses, the most notable coming in last year’s NWSL Championship.

“We haven't had the smoothest sailing at home this year, so to be able to go into some do or die games, like playoffs, and have this big win under our belt against an opponent that we have very deep history with, it feels good,” midfielder Hal Hershfelt said.

Washington will hope to ride the momentum of Saturday’s performance as it approaches its final two regular season games — at the Kansas City Current next week and at home against last-place Chicago on Nov. 1.

“It's a big statement for us to show that we can beat anyone in this league,” Morgan said. “If we apply ourselves in the right way, we can be a really, really dangerous team into these last, hopefully, five games.”

entries.title: Homan Says the Trump Administration Has a ‘Strong Case’ Against Rep. Ilhan Omar
entries.summary: Former President Barack Obama on Sunday called it a transparent effort to intimidate Omar.
entries.content:
White House border czar Tom Homan defended the raid on Rep. Ilhan Omar’s D.C. home last week, arguing that the federal government has a “strong case” against the Minnesota Democrat.

Homan told Fox News on Saturday he doesn’t want to get ahead of Homeland Security Investigations — the criminal investigative agency for U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement that led the raid — but he has “been told they have a strong case.”

“We’ll let the evidence lead where it leads but she’ll be held to the same standard you and I are held,” Homan said. “If she violated the law, then she’ll be held accountable.”

Federal agents raided Omar’s D.C. home on Oct. 12 and seized items including the congresswoman’s cellphone and passport. The raid is part of a probe into immigration fraud and questions about citizenship paperwork Omar’s late father prepared in 1995. Neither Omar or any of her family members have been charged in connection with the investigation, though several of her relatives have received grand jury subpoenas from the Justice Department.

Omar, who was born in Somalia and became a U.S. citizen in 2000, called the raid “an outrageous abuse of power” that had been conducted by President Donald Trump’s administration in an attempt to “intimidate his political enemies.”

Several prominent political figures have come to the Minnesota Democrat’s defense, including former President Barack Obama. He faced his own citizenship conspiracy theories known as the “birther” movement, which was perpetuated in large-part by Trump, despite being born in Hawaii. Obama said the president targeted Omar because “she has been one of the Trump Administration’s fiercest critics.”

“The fact that any president, or any administration, is willing to engage in such transparent efforts to intimidate someone should outrage all Americans, regardless of how they feel about Congresswoman Omar’s political views,” Obama wrote Sunday on X. “Because if this becomes the new normal, there’s no reason to believe it will stop with her — or that future presidents, in either party, won’t do the same.”

Homan’s comments echo remarks Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin made about the raid earlier this week. On Friday, Mullin told the "Charlie Kirk Show" that federal authorities had served multiple other search warrants on the same day as the raid on Omar’s home.

"She wasn't — or it wasn't the only place we served the warrant," Mullin said.

He added that the department and Trump did not and would not want to move forward with the operation “unless we knew that it couldn't be politically driven,” but said now Omar “wants to try making it about themselves.”

“This was about enforcing once again our nation's laws, and it's a strong case," Mullin said.

Omar has served four terms in the House, and she is the first Somali American elected to Congress. She is running for her fifth term for Minnesota’s 5th Congressional District.

entries.title: Trump Says East Potomac Renovation Will Begin Nov. 15
entries.summary: The president wrote in a social media post that the new golf course will have a “tremendously positive economic” impact on D.C.
entries.content:
President Donald Trump confirmed his much-discussed plans to build a “world championship” golf course at East Potomac Park in a social media post Sunday, despite an ongoing lawsuit aimed at halting the proposed overhaul.

The finished course will be open to the public, equipped to host high-level golf tournaments including the U.S. Open and have a “tremendously positive economic development impact” on D.C., creating “many jobs,” the president wrote on Truth Social. The post did not include any mention of costs.

Redevelopment, spearheaded by golf course architect Tom Fazio and Interior Secretary Doug Burgum, will begin Nov. 15, and end sometime in early 2028, Trump wrote. His post was accompanied by a rendering of an 18-hole golf course that covers the length of East Potomac, including the Hains Point recreational area.

The announcement comes just days after a federal judge ordered a halt to tree cutting at the golf course until next week. On Friday night, Justice Department lawyers asked for U.S. District Judge Ana C. Reyes to be removed from the case because she has shown “open hostility” toward the government.

Interior and the National Park Service are defendants in the lawsuit, brought by the D.C. Preservation League and local residents, who have long enjoyed the island park in southwest D.C. for its accessible golfing, tennis courts, playground, cycling and abundant green space.

“The recreation landscape [will be] so horrifically changed. If you think of all of the rides and races that happen in D.C. — from the D.C. bike ride, to the Army Ten-Miler to the Marine Corps marathon,” said Elizabeth Kiker, the executive director of Washington Area Bicycle Association. “There’s no room for biking, bird-watching, running, for all of the public uses that Hains Point has had for 100 years.”

Trump sees the park differently.

“The current course is old, broken, dilapidated, and of no further use or effect,” he wrote on Sunday. “It is in very poor condition, with falling, dangerous and disease infested trees and importantly, a collapsing and hazardous seawall.”

The National Park Service did not immediately respond to a request for comment. A hearing in the ongoing lawsuit is scheduled for Monday morning.

entries.title: Trump Endorses Embattled Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for Reelection
entries.summary: The coveted boost comes after the two leaders' strategies in the Middle East diverged.
entries.content:
By Michelle L. Price

WEST PALM BEACH, Fla. — President Donald Trump on Sunday endorsed embattled Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for reelection, a coveted boost because of Trump’s popularity but one that the U.S. leader withheld for months as their strategies in the Middle East diverged.

Trump said in a post on social media that Netanyahu “has been a Great Warrior Prime Minister, and an even greater Partner for Peace in combatting the Islamic Republic of Iran.”

Israelis are set to vote Oct. 27, in the first national elections since the 2023 Hamas attack on Israel.

The absence of an endorsement was a setback for the Likud party politician, who had billed his tight ties to Trump as a selling point for keeping him in power.
entries.author: The Associated Press

entries.title: Zelenskyy Warns That Trump Waiving Russian Sanctions Is ‘Strengthening Putin’s War’
entries.summary: The Ukrainian president decried Trump’s decision as U.S. Cabinet officials defended waiving the new, congressionally approved penalties on Russian oil.
entries.content:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy criticized President Donald Trump’s decision to waive sweeping new sanctions on Russia, a move Zelenskyy said is “strengthening Putin’s war.”

“It’s really big support for Putin. He feels victory with [the removed] sanctions.” Zelenskyy told NBC’s “Meet the Press” on Sunday — adding that Ukraine is concerned that the U.S. may do more to ease the pressure on Russia including reevaluating restrictions on Russian energy sources and frozen assets.

Congress passed new, substantial sanctions on Russia in September in honor of late Sen. Lindsey Graham — who was one of the most outspoken allies for Ukraine during the country's ongoing, four-year war against Russia’s invasion. Trump issued an executive order on Friday blocking the new penalties “in the national interests of the United States.”

Zelenskyy has faced strong criticism from Trump in recent weeks for continuing to strike Russian oil refineries and allegedly stalling peace negotiations to end the war. Trump has pinned skyrocketing global fuel prices in part on Ukraine’s strikes, but Zelenskyy repeatedly contends that the ongoing Iran war should bear the majority of blame.

Earlier this month, Trump announced a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin to import millions of tons of Russian diesel into the U.S., a move that compounded Zelenskyy’s concerns over the strength of U.S. support for Ukraine.

“If United States will support Putin, I mean, it's unbelievable. It's a tragedy. It’s a historic mistake and big tragedy,” Zelenskyy said Sunday — adding that if the U.S. takes Russia’s side “of course we will not prevail and we will not be able to stand.”

Zelenskyy told NBC that he still trusts Trump and the U.S., but he hopes that Trump “will change his decisions, change his attitude to Putin.”

The conflict between the two world leaders came to a head last week when Ukraine reported lapses in U.S. intelligence sharing and issues with technology contracted to Ukraine by the U.S. Department of Defense — allegations that the Trump administration has denied.

Ukraine stopped receiving U.S. intelligence, which can specifically provide an early warning when Russia uses ballistic missiles, for a period of three days, the Ukrainian president told NBC.

“It was blocked for some period of time,” Zelenskyy said. “And then it was deblocked by [the] American side. We are very thankful for this.”

Trump publicly denied that he or SpaceX founder Elon Musk, whose company develops the Starlink and Starshield satellite network used by Ukraine, ordered any restrictions on the technology for Ukraine's operations — an assertion Zelenskyy strongly refuted on Sunday.

“Of course the message came from [the U.S.] government,” Zelenskyy said. “It’s not my opinion. It’s [the] opinion of our generals, of our government, and of course also my opinion they say that it was the message from [the] American government to limit this speed, and technically SpaceX did it.”

He added that Ukraine is still experiencing speed limitations for its drone operations.

After Zelenskyy’s interview, NBC spoke with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent who said the Ukrainian president “should be very careful about making statements like this that aren’t true” when speaking about any alleged U.S. involvement in the Starlink and Starshield restrictions.

“President Trump and Secretary [of State Marco] Rubio have categorically said that no one under the Trump administration did that, and I think it is very reckless for President Zelenskyy to make such a charge,” Bessent said Sunday.

Bessent defended the president's move waiving the sanctions and called for tougher criticism on Ukraine’s allies in Europe that still import Russian resources — though the European Union’s overall reliance on Russia’s natural gas industry has dropped dramatically since the start of the war in 2022.

Bessent and Rubio pointed to Trump’s invocation of the statutory 60-day review period written into the Russian sanctions bill, which technically gives the administration until Dec. 16 to assess the penalties.

“The problem is these sanctions were not just sanctions on Russia. They include tariffs on a number of countries, India, for example, and others,” Rubio told reporters Saturday night at Joint Base Andrews before departing for Uzbekistan. “And so I think the president wants to take the 60-day period of time to sort of analyze what imposing both sanctions and tariffs will mean to the global economy and even to the U.S. economy.”

The White House has defended waiving the sanctions, asserting that enforcing the penalties could impede peace negotiations between Russia and Ukraine. Energy Secretary Chris Wright reiterated this position Sunday in an interview with CNN’s “State of the Union.”

“What President Trump is trying to do is find what different way will lead to peace,” Wright said. “He's always looking for innovations. This is quite innovative, actually.”

Mike Rogers, the Republican nominee for Senate in Michigan, appeared to break with Trump over waiving the sanctions, following the lead of several other Republicans outraged over the move.

Rogers told CNN “that's just not where I would be” and added that he would have voted for the sanctions bill if he was in the Senate. When asked if he was concerned that Trump’s recent moves to ease pressure on Russia make it appear that the U.S. is siding with Russia over Ukraine, Rogers said he does not believe Trump is siding with Russia.

“I do worry about the optics of it, but I understand what his motives are,” Rogers said. “And his motives are to try to get prices back down on diesel. Diesel is hurting us.”
entries.author: Jenna Monnin

entries.title: DHS Punts Decision to End Deportation Protections for Immigrants From Ukraine and Sudan
entries.summary: The Trump administration has also delayed ending temporary protections for immigrants from El Salvador.
entries.content:
More than 105,000 people from Ukraine and Sudan will keep their deportation protections that were set to end Monday, the Department of Homeland Security announced Sunday.

The move keeps those immigrants under the temporary protected status, which allows them to live and work in the U.S. Although that status was set to end Monday, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin did not issue an official decision to terminate TPS for Ukraine and Sudan.

DHS issued the same statement for both countries Sunday, saying that an announcement would be made at an appropriate time and Ukrainians and Sudanese people in the country under TPS would retain protection.

The announcement comes after DHS left immigrants from El Salvador in the same state of limbo after the designation expired for the Central American country last month. But the Trump administration, with the backing of the Supreme Court, has moved to wipe the temporary protection designations for most of the countries that had them, including by targeting Haitians who sought refuge in the U.S. after their protections ended in July.

Congress established TPS in 1990 to prevent deportations to countries deemed too unsafe because of armed conflict, natural disasters or other humanitarian crises.

Approximately 103,700 Ukrainians and 1,900 Sudanese people are beneficiaries of the program, according to DHS. The Biden administration granted TPS for Ukraine in 2022 because of the war with Russia, and Sudanese immigrants have had the status for nearly 30 years because of the ongoing armed conflict, displacement of millions inside the country and famine.

A bipartisan group of Senators had introduced a bill in September extending TPS for Ukrainians.

“The reality is that it is simply not safe for them to return to Ukraine,” Sen. Lisa Murkowski (R-Alaska) said in a statement announcing the legislation. “We should not force Ukrainians who we allowed into the U.S. and who are here legally and contributing to our communities back into an active war zone.”
entries.author: Jackie Llanos

entries.title: Republican Lieutenant Governor Candidate in Massachusetts Ends Campaign After Arrest
entries.summary: Shawn Oliver was arrested early Sunday in a suspected drunk driving crash.
entries.content:
NEW BEDFORD, Mass. — The Republican candidate for lieutenant governor in Massachusetts dropped out of the race on Sunday hours after he was arrested in a suspected drunk driving crash.

Shawn Oliver, a city councilor in New Bedford and a corrections officer, said in a post on X he was ending his campaign because "the election is too important to be overshadowed by personal matters.”

The move came after his running mate, Republican gubernatorial candidate Mike Minogue, said he asked Oliver to immediately suspend his campaign and that "when elected, I will formally ask for his resignation.”

“I am extremely disappointed,” Minogue said on X. “There is no excuse for driving under the influence.”

Police said Oliver was arrested after he was involved in a car crash late Saturday involving a vehicle that struck multiple parked vehicles before turning over.

The 42-year-old was taken to the hospital for injuries and arrested on suspicion of operating under the influence of alcohol, negligent operation of a motor vehicle, a marked lanes violation and speeding, police spokesperson Holly Huntoon said in an email.

New Bedford Mayor Jon Mitchell, a Democrat, said the allegations against Oliver were “deeply concerning” and that the public deserves to hear from him about what happened.

A phone message seeking comment was left for Oliver, who was born and raised in the city of 100,000 people about 60 miles (97 kilometers) south of Boston and was elected to the city council in 2023.

Minogue, a businessman and military veteran, faces incumbent Democratic Gov. Maura Healey on the November ballot. The Democratic candidate for lieutenant governor is incumbent Kim Driscoll.

The lieutenant governor's position in Massachusetts is seen as largely ceremonial, but the officeholder is first in line to become governor if the governor resigns or dies.

Oliver has been placed on restricted work duty at his job at the Massachusetts Treatment Center “while all facts and circumstances are reviewed,” Lindsay Corcoran, a spokesperson for the state's Department of Correction, said in an email. The medium-security facility houses sex offenders and people civilly committed as sexually dangerous persons.
